title: Asymmetric Cavity Bounds with Frozen Outer Mirrors
scientific_hypothesis: Decoupling the central defect cavity (layers 8-10) from the outer mirror stack (layers 0-7, 11-20) by freezing outer mirror thicknesses and applying asymmetric bounds to the cavity region will allow layer 10 to converge to the 1550 nm half-wave resonance condition (optical thickness ~380-430 nm) without destabilizing the visible stopband edges, improving the dual-band target score beyond 0.7731.
design_principle: Freeze peripheral mirror layers that have accumulated visible-band reflectance margin; constrain central cavity layer optical thickness to half-wave resonance at 1550 nm; allow adjacent transition layers to optimize for impedance matching between frozen mirrors and tuned cavity.
proposed_topology: 21-layer stack: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2(cavity)|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2 on fused silica substrate, air incident. Layers 0-7 frozen at previous best values, layers 8-10 optimized with layer 10 optical thickness bounded 380-430 nm, layers 11-20 free optimization.
design_variables: Layer 10 thickness (HfO2 cavity, optical thickness 380-430 nm)
soft_objectives: Maintain target score improvement over 0.7731 baseline
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 compatible with ion-assisted deposition
Frozen outer layers reduce fabrication sensitivity in mirror regions
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance requires half-wave optical thickness at target wavelength
Freezing optimized mirror layers preserves accumulated stopband performance
Asymmetric cavity bounds decouple resonance tuning from mirror optimization
expected_advantages: Faster convergence to 1550 nm resonance without disturbing visible stopband
Reduced optimization dimensionality in frozen regions
Clear separation of cavity and mirror design responsibilities
known_risks: Frozen layers may prevent global optimum if mirror-cavity coupling is significant
Optical thickness constraint may be too restrictive for actual resonance condition
Layer 10 bounds may conflict with adjacent layer impedance matching requirements
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer HfO2/SiO2 defect-cavity stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2. Freeze layers 0-7 at thicknesses [250.6, 306.5, 256.0, 300.9, 269.6, 278.7, 239.9, 252.1] nm from previous best candidate. Constrain layer 10 (central HfO2 cavity) optical thickness to 380-430 nm range. Optimize layers 8-9 and 11-20 with gradient-based optimizer. Evaluate transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and reflectance in 400-700 nm band at normal incidence. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: asymmetric cavity bounds on layers 8-10 with layer 10 optical thickness forced to 380-430 nm window; frozen outer mirror layers 0-7 to preserve visible stopband margin accumulated in prior iterations.
